title: One executive, several unrelated City contractors
question: Which named chief executives, finance officers or operating officers appear at two or more unrelated City contractors, and at the same time?
finding: 57 rare names are listed as chief executive, finance or operating officer on the notices of two or more contractors that share no other officers; for 2 the date ranges overlap by more than three months, and 4 share a name with a former City employee.
how: Chief executive, finance and operating officers on the contract notices, grouped by contractor; contractors sharing three or more names, a name stem or a parent are treated as one. The overlap is between the first and last notice naming the person at each.
limits: Most rows are a career move, a merger, or an interim finance chief brought in after trouble, which is a repair, not a problem. Notices keep old names, so overlaps are overstated. The use of the list is to see which pairs of contractors have had the same hand on the books.

rows.match: Same name on each contractor’s notice (rare name). The records do not show whether this is the same person or two people with the same name; each organization’s own return or roster would settle it.
